newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Boeing not seen issue at EU/US summit - US officials.
newsitem.headline: Boeing not seen issue at EU/US summit - US officials.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton is not expected to raise the issue of the merger of Boeing and McDonnell Douglas at a summit with the European Union next week, U.S. officials said on Thursday.

The officials, who asked not to be named, said the merger was still being investigated in both the United States and Brussels and that until they were completed U.S. politicians were likely to keep out of the issues formally.
"The president will be hard put to comment because we are still looking at it," one official said, referring to the investigation by the U.S. Federal Trade Commission.
He said the two probes had different aims -- one to study the effect of the merger in the United States, the other on industry in the European Union.
Washington did not question the Commission's legal competency to study its part of the deal, the official said, adding that he hoped both probes would come to the same conclusion on the deal (JMG)

Clinton holds his twice-yearly summit with the EU on May 28 in the Hague. The EU will be represented by European Commission President Jacques Santer and Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok. -- Brussels newsroom: +32 2 287-6830
